proposals.rationale: Soft hypothesis: reducing the 12 h heated reaction interval to the existing 2 min duration may leave insufficient time for productive C–H borylation.
Soft hypothesis: raising the reaction temperature to the existing 90 °C process temperature could increase substrate, product, or catalyst degradation relative to the reported 80 °C condition.

Soft hypothesis: deleting the provisional reactor-to-heater connection represents loss of thermal coupling, which may prevent the reaction mixture from attaining or maintaining the intended heated condition.
Soft hypothesis: omitting the argon-atmosphere step may expose the moisture- and air-sensitive base, diboron reagent, or iridium catalyst system to deactivating contaminants.
